module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Sqrt
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Clique
public import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Finite
public import Mathlib.Data.ENat.Lattice
public import Mathlib.Data.Multiset.Sort
public import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
public import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
public import Mathlib.Order.CompletePartialOrder

@[expose] public section

namespace SimpleGraph

variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The average degree of `G`. -/
noncomputable def averageDegree (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℚ  :=
  (∑ v, (G.degree v : ℚ)) / (Fintype.card α : ℚ)

/-- The multiset of degrees of a graph. -/
def degreeMultiset (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : Multiset ℕ :=
  Finset.univ.val.map fun v => G.degree v

/-- The degree sequence of a graph, sorted in nondecreasing order. -/
noncomputable def degreeSequence (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : List ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.val.map fun v : α => G.degree v).sort (· ≤ ·)

/--
The maximum number of occurrences of any term of the degree sequence of `G`.
-/
noncomputable def degreeSequenceMultiplicity (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  letI degs := degreeSequence G
  (List.max? (degs.map (fun d => degs.count d))).getD 0

/-- Infinite graphs: definitions for max degree and clique number so that the maximum
degree of a graph with unbounded degree is
`∞` rather than 0.
-/
noncomputable
def edegree {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) (v : V) : ℕ∞ := (G.neighborSet v).encard

noncomputable
def emaxDegree {V : Type*} (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ∞ := ⨆ v, G.edegree v

/-- Cardinality of the union of the neighbourhoods of the ends of the non-edge `e`. -/
def non_edge_neighborhood_card (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (e : Sym2 α) : ℕ :=
  Sym2.lift ⟨fun u v => (G.neighborFinset u ∪ G.neighborFinset v).card,
    fun u v => by simp [Finset.union_comm]⟩ e

/-- Minimum size of the neighbourhood of a non-edge of `G`. -/
noncomputable def NG (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℝ :=
  let non_edges := (compl G).edgeFinset
  if h : non_edges.Nonempty then
    let neighbor_sizes := non_edges.image (non_edge_neighborhood_card G)
    (neighbor_sizes.min' (Finset.Nonempty.image h _))
  else
    (Fintype.card α : ℝ)

noncomputable def S (G : SimpleGraph α) : ℝ :=
  open scoped Classical in
  let card := Fintype.card α
  if card < 2 then 0 else
    let degrees := Multiset.ofList (List.map (fun v => G.degree v) Finset.univ.toList)
    let sorted_degrees := degrees.sort (· ≤ ·)
    ↑((sorted_degrees[card - 2]?).getD 0)

/-- The **second-smallest degree** of `G`'s degree sequence — DeLaVina's `σ(G)`
per the WOWII definitions popup (defEntry 65): "order the degree sequence in
nondecreasing order `d₁ ≤ d₂ ≤ … ≤ dₙ`, the second smallest degree of the
sequence is the 2nd entry". For graphs with `n ≤ 1` we conventionally
return `0`. -/
noncomputable def secondSmallestDegree (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℕ :=
  (degreeSequence G).getD 1 0

/-- The number of triangles (3-cliques) of `G` incident to vertex `v`:
the number of 3-element cliques containing `v`. -/
noncomputable def numTrianglesAtVertex (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (v : α) : ℕ :=
  ((G.cliqueFinset 3).filter (fun s => v ∈ s)).card

/-- The length of a graph: the square root of the sum of the squares of degrees. -/
noncomputable def degreeL2Norm (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] : ℝ :=
  Real.sqrt (∑ v, (G.degree v : ℝ) ^ 2)

/-- The number of vertices of degree k in `G`. -/
def countDegreeK (G : SimpleGraph α) [DecidableRel G.Adj] (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (Finset.univ.filter (fun v => G.degree v = k)).card

end SimpleGraph

reformulations.difference: The Lean statement clears the denominator and explicitly assumes that the second-smallest degree is positive.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a finite connected graph with at least two vertices, every degree is positive and the degree sequence has at least two entries. Consequently secondSmallestDegree is positive, so the additional hypothesis is redundant. Division by this positive real number gives exactly the equivalence between (girth + 1) / σ ≤ tree and girth + 1 ≤ tree * σ. Both positivity and this inequality equivalence were proved in /workspace/review/sigma_inequality.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses extended-natural invariants on arbitrary graphs and states 2 * χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2 instead of a ceiling inequality for finite graph invariants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural χ, ω, Δ, χ ≤ ceil((ω + Δ + 1)/2) is exactly equivalent to 2χ ≤ ω + Δ + 2; this arithmetic equivalence and finite agreement of emaxDegree with maxDegree were proved in Lean. The extension to arbitrary graphs is equivalent to the finite conjecture: if Δ = ∞ the Lean inequality is automatic; otherwise clique sizes are bounded and the finite conjecture supplies a uniform finite coloring bound for every finite subgraph. The de Bruijn–Erdős theorem supplies that coloring for the whole graph. The converse follows by restriction to finite graphs. The complete graph-level equivalence was not formalized in the scratch files.

reformulations.difference: The cited question concerns triangle-free graphs of maximum degree at most six; Lean assumes maximum degree exactly six and clique number exactly two.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Given any triangle-free graph of maximum degree at most six, its disjoint union with K₁,₆ has maximum degree exactly six and clique number exactly two. A five-coloring of the union restricts to the original graph. Conversely, the finite maximum-degree bound ensures bounded clique sizes, so Mathlib's natural-valued cliqueNum has no unbounded-supremum default problem: cliqueNum = 2 really implies triangle-freeness. Thus the exact-value formulation is equivalent to the at-most formulation.

reformulations.difference: NG returns the number of vertices when there are no nonedges, whereas the source writes a minimum over nonedges without specifying an empty-family value.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For noncomplete graphs, NG is precisely the source's minimum of |N(u) ∪ N(v)| over distinct nonadjacent vertices. For Kₙ with n ≥ 2, the added case is n − 1 ≤ Ls(Kₙ), which is automatic from a spanning star (K₂ has two leaves). Thus this totalization adds only an automatic case to the source inequality. The original 1996 proof likewise starts by assuming diameter greater than one.

reformulations.difference: The source explicitly requires n > 1, while the Lean theorem permits a connected singleton graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Connectedness excludes the empty graph, so the only additional case is K₁. It has no total dominating set; consequently IsWellTotallyDominated, which universally compares minimal total dominating sets, holds vacuously. This singleton case was proved in /workspace/review/nonedge_and_singleton.lean. Adding it does not change the universal problem on graphs of order greater than one; the full quantified equivalence was not proved in Lean.

review.notes:
No substantiated mathematical defect was found in the 13 target definitions. In particular, S matches WOWII's uppercase Σ (definition 72), not its lowercase σ (definition 65). Lean proofs verify degree-sequence length, sorting and multiplicity preservation; the characterization degreeSequenceMultiplicity ≤ m iff every degree frequency is ≤ m; agreement of finite and extended degrees; and infinity for unbounded locally finite degrees. Tests cover empty and singleton graphs, complete graphs, paths, the paw graph, overlapping neighborhoods, and infinite graphs. All eight scratch Lean files compile without errors or admitted proofs. No checkout files were edited.

Live WOWII access timed out, and Erdős Problems returned 403 despite a descriptive User-Agent; archived primary pages were used. Their dates limit current-status verification. Archived open labels on the proof-tagged WOWII statements do not by themselves establish that the Lean statuses are stale; #20 also has inconsistent archived HTML/JavaScript status labels. No unsupported status correction is proposed.

The remaining source limitation is the full 1991 Erdős–Fajtlowicz–Staton paper. Its metadata was accessible, but its text was not. The affected use-site comparisons are listed below; this does not affect the proved interpretation of the library's degree multiplicity.
